title: Give a dial turn on the workbench a sound, sourced free with its rights and provenance written down
tier_reason: A UI sound behind the integration suite; git reverts it. The pick between candidates is the CEO's, made on a decision card he can listen to, as the standing rule for sourcing sound says.
ask: The CEO, 2026-09-10, after the training workbench (docs/design/14-training-workbench.md, built as v0.2.2) landed with no sound on its dials: 'Can you add a dial sound? Maybe ask our SFX agent to find a published sound with permissive sound rights for us to use, like we did before? And follow the normal procedure for attributing the file provenance.' The standing rule for this seat (hq/data/staff/dmitri/memory.md, 2026-09-04): free-to-use sounds first; candidates come back as a decision card he can listen to, each with its source URL and licence; CREDITS.md is written in the same change that adds the file. The precedent is the harvest sound: three CC0 recordings from Freesound fetched by tools/fetch_sfx_candidates.py (which refuses anything not CC0 and writes assets/audio/sfx/CANDIDATES.json), credited in CREDITS.md around lines 417-423. The dial: ui/workbench_dials.gd — minus and plus buttons and a held pip (hold_pip) emit the verb tune through farm.apply_action (around line 264); a button at its end of the ladder is disabled. Sounds are registered in systems/audio_manager.gd's table (line 29, preloads) and played with AudioManager.play_sfx(name); the shop plays 'jingle' on a purchase at ui/menus.gd:865; AudioManager.last_sfx (line 49) records the last name played, so a test can read it.
source_message: CEO, 2026-09-10: add a dial sound; have the SFX seat find a published sound with permissive rights, as before, and follow the provenance procedure.
result: Landed on main. Three CC0 recordings from Freesound fetched under the dial slot and kept with their sources and licences (CANDIDATES.json, CREDITS.md): 'dial turn' by freemaster2 (#120844) is wired as the game's dial sound and plays only after an accepted tune, for the buttons and the held pip alike; 'Switch Klunk 2' (#556634) and 'Metronome click 2' (#793345) sit unwired as the other options on decision card Q-102, which the CEO can listen to. The dials scenario asserts the sound on an accepted turn and silence on a disabled one. The seat's session was cut off by a usage limit after the work was done; the chief of staff applied the held patch, corrected two phrases, and verified the suites (unit 2540; integration green but for one unrelated timing-flaky scenario, fixed separately).
